subject: left-handed people
one_liner: A collaborative interface design tool that loads every file mirrored, so your drawing hand never sits on top of the work.
brand_voice_notes: Swiss design-tool corporate. Flat, declarative, faintly self-satisfied. Verso talks about handedness the way an infrastructure company talks about latency: a measured constraint with an obvious fix. The fix is wrong. Never winks. Never explains the joke. Treats right-handed people as a supported but read-only population, and treats paper as a competitor with better palm dynamics.

hero.h1: The canvas was on the wrong side.
hero.sub: Verso is a collaborative interface design tool that loads every file mirrored and keeps the toolbar on the right. Your hand sits beside the work instead of across it. Right-handed collaborators are welcome to comment.

features.title: Mirrored Canvas
features.blurb: Every file opens flipped on the vertical axis, so your hand rests beside the artboard instead of over it. Exports ship flipped as well. Most clients adjust inside a quarter.

features.title: Handedness SSO
features.blurb: Onboarding runs a forty-second scissors assessment. Verified left-handers receive edit rights. Everyone else receives comment access and a weekly digest of what they missed.

features.title: The Smudge Layer
features.blurb: A top layer that renders graphite drag beneath your cursor in real time. It cannot be hidden, flattened, or deleted. Parity with paper was the entire brief.

demo_screen_concept: A mirrored Verso editor. Toolbar, layers list, and properties inspector are all pinned to the right edge; the artboard sits left and is rendered flipped. Three collaborator avatars carry handedness-verification badges (two verified, one pending, one of them visibly right-handed and marked read-only). The layers list toggles visibility per layer except Smudge Layer, whose eye control is disabled with a tooltip. Moving the cursor across the artboard leaves a permanent stepped graphite smudge that has no clear control. A tool rail switches between Move, Frame, Pen, Palm, and Text, each changing the inspector contents. The X coordinate field counts leftward from the right edge and cannot be set to a positive number. A prominent Flip Back button opens a modal requiring a fresh handedness re-assessment, which offers only one selectable option.

images.rationale: Hero skipped because the direction is mirrored Swiss modernist, which is purely typographic: a photograph would soften the grid poster and fight the ultramarine floods. Demo subject assets skipped because demo_screen_concept is a design-editor console (tool rail, layers list, inspector) and not photo-shaped. Full budget went to the three testimonial headshots, deadpan corporate portraits of left-handed professionals against the paper ground, which is the always-applicable slot. Three of a possible four images generated; the fourth was left unspent rather than manufactured. Judge note: all three subjects hold the pencil in their right hand as rendered, so the landing page mirrors the headshots with scaleX(-1), which corrects the handedness and matches the site's mirror conceit.

design_direction.style: Mirrored Swiss modernist design-tool site, paper daylight mode. The page is staged as the product site of a heavily funded collaborative design company that has decided handedness is an unsolved layout problem and files reaching across your own artboard under latency. A flat paper ground (#F1F1EE) runs the whole page with no gradients, no texture, no glow, no shadows, and no rounded corners: every corner is 0px and every division is a 1px ink hairline or a solid flood of color, so the page reads as an International Style grid poster rather than a website. The organizing move is the mirror: the entire layout is right-anchored. The wordmark sits at the far right of the header and the nav sits left of it; headlines, section labels, feature columns, and pricing tiers all read right to left, with the most expensive tier first and section numerals counting down (05 04 03 02 01) so the eye is forced to start where it usually stops. The core motif is the flipped glyph: display numerals and the leading letter of the wordmark are rendered mirrored with scaleX(-1), never explained, so the page keeps quietly showing you type the wrong way round. The second motif is the smudge band: a hard-edged stepped grey bar built from repeating-linear-gradient in solid steps (no blur, no soft gradient) that hems section breaks and sits under key figures like graphite dragged by a palm. One ultramarine (#1F2ED6) carries the wordmark block, every primary CTA, the mirror axis rule, and one word per headline, always as a solid flood with paper knocked out of it; one rationed fuchsia (#D6006B) is reserved strictly for handedness telemetry (verification states, the pending badge, the read-only stamp on right-handed collaborators, live seat counts) and appears nowhere else. Archivo sets the wordmark and headlines in tight heavy grotesque caps with design-tool-that-raised-a-D confidence; Figtree carries plain, faintly release-note body copy. Every figure that pretends to be workspace telemetry (verified hands, smudge coverage percentages, re-flip queue depth, tier prices, X coordinates) is set in DM Mono with tabular figures inside hairline-ruled paper wells, so it reads like the inspector, not marketing. Motion is grid-restrained: the mirror axis draws down once on load, plates invert to ultramarine flood on hover with the hairline vanishing, CTAs shift 2px left on press (never right), the pending verification dot pulses on a 4s cycle, sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No dark mode, no glass, no blur, no clay shadow pairs, no soft gradients, no bento lattice, no didone engraving, no catalog stitching, no sticker offset shadows, no HUD brackets, no nautical chrome, no storefront capsules, no engraved seals, no emoji. Reads like a company that files your dominant hand under 'render order' and considers paper a competitor with better palm dynamics.
design_direction.archetype: Collaborative design-tool product page, mirrored: right-anchored typographic hero with a monumental grotesque headline and a CSS-built mirrored editor plate, a telemetry strip of verified-hand figures, three feature columns numbered in descending order, testimonial plates with headshots and verification badges, a pricing ladder running most expensive first, closing CTA band, handoff to the mirrored editor demo.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Mirror axis draws top to bottom once on load (600ms, ease-out). Plates invert to an ultramarine flood on hover in 180ms with the hairline border dropping to transparent. Primary CTAs translate 2px to the left on press, never right. The pending-verification dot pulses opacity on a 4s cycle. Section content fades up 6px with a 40ms per-child stagger on first scroll into view. Smudge bands do not animate. Everything above is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Full-bleed paper. A 1px ultramarine vertical mirror axis sits at 38% from the left and runs the full viewport height behind everything. Right of the axis: an eyebrow label in wide-tracked mono caps, then the headline set right-aligned at clamp(2.6rem, 7vw, 5.6rem) in Archivo 800 with tight tracking and the word 'wrong' knocked out of an ultramarine flood, then the sub paragraph capped at 46ch, then the primary CTA as a solid ultramarine block with a square 44px hit area minimum. Left of the axis, a monumental mirrored numeral 01 in outlined display type bleeds off the left edge at 30% opacity. Below the fold line, a full-width hairline-ruled telemetry strip carries four mono figures with tabular numerals. Header is inverted: nav links left, wordmark hard right, single hairline underneath. On viewports under 760px the axis moves to 16px from the left, the headline stays right-aligned, and the bleeding numeral is dropped.
